title: Pure dimension of fibres of a flat family with dense pure-dimensional generic fibre
statement: Let $S$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and let $f:X\to S$ be a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose that the generic fibre $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is dense in $X$ and that, for an integer $d\geq0$, every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X_\eta$ has Krull dimension $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then every nonempty fibre $X_s$ is pure of dimension $d$, meaning that each of its irreducible components has dimension $d$. The same holds for every nonempty geometric fibre $X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, where $s\in S$ and $\Omega$ is any algebraically closed extension of its residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-fibre-product]. The empty scheme is allowed as $X$, in which case the conclusions are vacuous.
